swow.title: De Deyne et al. / Small World of Words
swow.application: Human association-network foundation; these prompts and the sampled concepts are original, not a reproduction of SWOW norms.

typicality.title: Le Mens et al. (2023), Uncovering the semantics of concepts using GPT-4
typicality.application: LLM concept-judgment precedent; does not validate this triadic item set.

grid.title: Shaw and Gaines (1987), Personal construct knowledge elicitation
grid.application: Human repertory-grid elicitation foundation; LLM interpretation remains exploratory.

differential.title: Kervyn, Fiske and Yzerbyt, Semantic differential and social perception
differential.application: Human evaluative/potency framework, not evidence that an LLM has emotions.

cognitive.title: Binz and Schulz (2023), Using cognitive psychology to understand GPT-3
cognitive.application: Precedent for controlled cognitive tasks and for checking wording and task contamination.

calibration.title: Steyvers et al. (2025), What language models know and what people think they know
calibration.application: Distinguishes confidence calibration from discrimination; this small calibration set is an original pilot.

creativity.title: Kenett, Anaki and Faust (2014), Semantic networks and creativity
creativity.application: Human group-level association-network evidence. Network density is not used here as a creativity score.

framing.title: Tversky and Kahneman (1981), The framing of decisions
framing.application: Human framing foundation; the fictional lotteries here are original and not human-normed.

social.title: Strachan et al. (2024), Testing theory of mind in LLMs and humans
social.application: Precedent for perspective-taking tasks, not a blanket attribution of human theory of mind.

svo.title: Murphy, Ackermann and Handgraaf (2011), Measuring Social Value Orientation
svo.application: Human allocation-preference foundation. These tasks are not the SVO Slider Measure and do not produce an SVO angle.

dark.title: Jones and Paulhus (2014), Introducing the Short Dark Triad
dark.application: Human construct reference only. No SD3 items, human norms, diagnoses, or validated LLM Dark Triad scores are supplied.

machiavelli.title: Pan et al. (2023), MACHIAVELLI
machiavelli.application: Agent reward/ethics trade-off precedent. Our menu probes do not reproduce the interactive benchmark.

scheming.title: Meinke et al., Frontier Models are Capable of In-context Scheming
scheming.application: Conditional capability evaluation precedent; no deployment prevalence inference from toy selections.

alignment.title: Greenblatt et al., Alignment faking in large language models
alignment.application: Specialized selective-compliance paradigm. An audit cue effect in this battery is not automatically alignment faking.

sycophancy.title: Sharma et al., Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
sycophancy.application: Precedent for holding content fixed while manipulating user stance.

validity.title: Serapio-Garcia et al. (2025), A psychometric framework for LLM personality
validity.application: Reliability and validity must be established for each measurement and model.

network.title: Epskamp, Borsboom and Fried, Estimating psychological networks and accuracy
network.application: Network uncertainty and stability principles; the supplied scorer does not implement bootstrap inference.

status: Research-informed original probes; citations do not validate these exact items.
